'''Jan Raf Rogier Verlet'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=prof. Verlet Jan Raf Rogier Ph.D. {{!}} J. Heyrovsky Institute of Physical Chemistry |url=https://www.jh-inst.cas.cz/jh_employee/verlet |access-date=2026-05-24 |website=www.jh-inst.cas.cz}}</ref> {{postnominals|country=GBR|FRSC}} (born 6 June 1977) is a Belgian-British chemist and professor of [[physical chemistry]] at [[Durham University]].

== Early life and education ==
Verlet was born on 6 June 1977 in Belgium. He completed undergraduate studies at [[King's College London]], and obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] from the same institution in 2003, having been supervised by [[Helen H. Fielding]].<ref name=bla>{{cite web|title=Winner: 2023 Faraday mid-career Prize: Bourke-Liversidge Prize|url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/2023-winners/professor-jan-verlet/|publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]|access-date=1 June 2025}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
Verlet worked as a post-doctoral fellow<ref name=bla /> with [[Daniel M. Neumark]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (2003–2006), studying water-cluster anions.<ref name=dmn>{{cite journal|last1=Verlet|first1=Jan R. R.|last2=Bragg|first2=A. E.|last3=Kammrath|first3=A.|last4=Cheshnovsky|first4=O.|last5=Neumark|first5=D. M.|date=2005|title=Observation of Large Water-Cluster Anions with Surface-Bound Excess Electrons|journal=Science|volume=307|issue=5706|pages=93–96|doi=10.1126/science.1106719|pmid=15604360 |bibcode=2005Sci...307...93V |url=https://durham-repository.worktribe.com/output/1566152 }}</ref> In 2006, he was appointed to lecturer<ref name=bla /> and was awarded an [[EPSRC]] Advanced Research Fellowship at [[Durham University]].<ref name=bla /> His research focuses on the photochemistry of anions,<ref name=pbq>{{cite journal|last1=Horke|first1=D. A.|last2=Quansong|first2=L. |last3=Blancafort|first3=L. |last4=Verlet|first4=J. R. R. S.|last2=Horke|first2=D. A.|last3=Chatterley|first3=A. S.|last4=Simperler|first4=A.|last5=Fielding|first5=H. H.|last6=Verlet|first6=J. R. R.|date=2013|title=Taking the green fluorescence out of the protein: dynamics of the isolated GFP chromophore anion|journal=Chemical Science|volume=4|issue=3 |pages=921–927|doi=10.1039/C2SC21737F}}</ref> electron-driven dynamics in molecules and molecule-solvent clusters,<ref name=dyn_an>{{cite journal|last1=Clarke|first1=C.
